description:
What is unclear and for whom: pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:350-386 declares a test that loops over a cases table of (ErrorKind, &str) pairs and asserts label_for and kind_for invert each other on each pair. The cases table at lines 356-377 is hand-written and lists exactly the 20 variants the helper code at lines 289-344 enumerates.

A new contributor reading this test will conclude: 'this tests the round-trip is bidirectional for every recognized variant.' That is the test's stated purpose ('the table is the oracle' — line 355).

But the test cannot catch the bug where a NEW stdlib ErrorKind variant exists outside this table. Adding ErrorKind::HostUnreachable to label_for but forgetting to update the test cases would still pass; removing kind_for's NotFound arm but also removing the cases entry for NotFound would still pass. The 'oracle' is the same hand-written table the code uses.

This is not a coverage problem of the test itself — the test is correct for what it claims. The problem is the test's name and comment suggest more than it delivers, and a reader updating the helper might believe 'this test will tell me if I forget to update the helper.' It will not.

What would make it clear: rename the test to label_table_is_self_consistent or label_round_trip_for_listed_variants, and add a comment 'this test only exercises variants enumerated in the cases table; coverage for new stdlib variants is the maintainer's manual responsibility — see PKIX-o3op.4.'

Coupled to PKIX-o3op.4 (the maintainer-burden finding).
title: Test label_round_trip_covers_recognized_variants is tautological as written
